        Handle player action with thread safety for multiplayer.

                return False, "Team has no active players!"
            
            if self.state.get_current_team().id != team_id:

                    return self._handle_collect_treasure(team, env)
                elif action == ActionType.USE_ABILITY:
                    return self._handle_use_ability(team, data)
                elif action == ActionType.LEAVE_GAME:
                    return self._handle_leave_game(team, data)
                else:
                    return False, "Invalid action!"
            except Exception as e:
                return False, f"Error processing action: {str(e)}"
    
    def _handle_move(self, team: Team, data: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Handle movement to next environment."""
        if data is None or 'environment' not in data:
            return False, "Missing environment data"
        
        try:
            next_env = EnvironmentType(data['environment'])
        except ValueError:
            return False, "Invalid environment"
        
        # Check if team can move (all puzzles solved in current environment)
        current_env = self.state.environments[team.current_environment]
        if current_env.get_unsolved_puzzles():
            return False, "Solve all puzzles before moving!"
        
        team.current_environment = next_env
        self.state.advance_turn()
        return True, f"Moved to {next_env.value}"
    
    def _handle_solve_puzzle(self, team: Team, env: Environment, 
                            data: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Handle puzzle solving attempt."""
        if data is None or 'puzzle_id' not in data:
            return False, "Missing puzzle ID"
        
        puzzle_id = data['puzzle_id']
        puzzle = next((p for p in env.puzzles if p.id == puzzle_id), None)

            return True, f"Solved puzzle: {puzzle.description}"
        else:

            return False, f"Failed to solve puzzle: {puzzle.description}"

        return True, f"Collected {treasures_to_collect} treasures!"
    
    def _handle_use_ability(self, team: Team, data: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Handle special ability usage."""
        if data is None or 'ability' not in data:
            return False, "Missing ability data"
        
        try:
            ability = Ability(data['ability'])
        except ValueError:
            return False, "Invalid ability"
        
        if not team.has_ability(ability):
            return False, f"No player in team has {ability.value} ability"
        
        # Ability usage might provide advantages in future turns
        self.state.advance_turn()
        return True, f"Used {ability.value} ability to gain advantage!"
    
    def _handle_leave_game(self, team: Team, data: Dict) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Handle player leaving the game."""
        if data is None or 'player_id' not in data:
            return False, "Missing player ID"
        
        player_id = data['player_id']
        player = next((p for p in team.players if p.id == player_id), None)
        
        if not player:
            return False, "Player not found"
        
        player.active = False
        
        # Check if team still has active players
        if not team.get_active_players():
            team.score = 0  # Team eliminated
        
        self.state.advance_turn()
        return True, f"Player {player.name} left the game"
    
    def _check_game_end(self, team: Team):
        """Check if game should end and determine winner."""
        if team.current_environment == EnvironmentType.FINAL_CHAMBER:
            # Calculate final scores for all teams
            end_time = time.time()
            for t in self.state.teams:
                t.score = t.calculate_score(end_time)
            
            # Determine winner (team with highest score)
            self.state.winner = max(self.state.teams, key=lambda t: t.score)
            self.state.game_over = True
    
    def get_game_status(self) -> Dict:
        """Get current game status for display."""
        if not self.state:
            return {"status": "Game not initialized"}
        
        status = {
            "current_turn": self.state.current_turn,
            "current_team": self.state.get_current_team().name,
            "game_over": self.state.game_over,
            "teams": []
        }
        
        if self.state.winner:
            status["winner"] = self.state.winner.name
        
        for team in self.state.teams:
            team_info = {
                "name": team.name,
                "environment": team.current_environment.value,
                "active_players": len(team.get_active_players()),
                "treasures_collected": team.treasures_collected,
                "score": team.score
            }
            status["teams"].append(team_info)
        
        return status

"""

import random

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

# ==================== ENUMS AND DATA CLASSES ====================

class WeaponType(Enum):

class ObjectiveType(Enum):

class PowerUpType(Enum):
    """Types of power-ups available in the arena."""
    HEALTH_BOOST = "health_boost"
    DAMAGE_BOOST = "damage_boost"
    SPEED_BOOST = "speed_boost"
    SHIELD = "shield"

class HazardType(Enum):

class DifficultyLevel(Enum):

@dataclass
class Weapon:
    """Represents a weapon with specific attributes."""
    name: str
    weapon_type: WeaponType
    damage: float
    range: float
    fire_rate: float  # attacks per second
    ammo_capacity: int
    current_ammo: int = field(init=False)
    
    def __post_init__(self):
        self.current_ammo = self.ammo_capacity
    
    def can_fire(self) -> bool:
        """Check if weapon has ammo to fire."""
        return self.current_ammo > 0
    
    def fire(self) -> float:
        """Fire the weapon and return damage dealt."""
        if self.can_fire():
            self.current_ammo -= 1
            return self.damage
        return 0.0
    
    def reload(self) -> None:
        """Reload the weapon to full capacity."""
        self.current_ammo = self.ammo_capacity


@dataclass
class PowerUp:
    """Represents a power-up in the arena."""
    powerup_type: PowerUpType
    position: Tuple[float, float]
    duration: float  # seconds
    value: float

    def apply(self, robot: 'Robot') -> None:
        """Apply power-up effects to a robot."""
        if not self.active:

        if self.powerup_type == PowerUpType.HEALTH_BOOST:
            robot.health = min(robot.max_health, robot.health + self.value)
        elif self.powerup_type == PowerUpType.DAMAGE_BOOST:
            robot.damage_multiplier *= self.value
        elif self.powerup_type == PowerUpType.SPEED_BOOST:
            robot.speed_multiplier *= self.value
        elif self.powerup_type == PowerUpType.SHIELD:
            robot.shield = self.value
        elif self.powerup_type == PowerUpType.AMMO_REFILL:
            for weapon in robot.weapons:
                weapon.reload()
        
        self.active = False


@dataclass
class Hazard:

    hazard_type: HazardType
    position: Tuple[float, float]

    active: bool = True
    
    def affects_position(self, position: Tuple[float, float]) -> bool:
        """Check if a position is within the hazard's area of effect."""
        dx = position[0] - self.position[0]
        dy = position[1] - self.position[1]
        distance = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
        return distance <= self.radius


@dataclass
class Objective:

    def update_progress(self, delta: float) -> None:
        """Update objective progress."""
        self.progress = max(0.0, min(1.0, self.progress + delta))
        if self.progress >= 1.0:
            self.completed = True


# ==================== ROBOT BASE CLASS ====================

class Robot(ABC):
    """Base class for all AI-controlled robots."""
    
    def __init__(self, robot_id: int, team: int, position: Tuple[float, float]):

            Weapon("Energy Blade", WeaponType.MELEE, 40.0, 3.0, 1.5, -1),  # -1 for infinite
            Weapon("Grenade Launcher", WeaponType.EXPLOSIVE, 60.0, 30.0, 0.5, 5)
        ]

        pass
    
    def move_toward(self, target: Tuple[float, float], delta_time: float) -> None:
        """Move the robot toward a target position."""
        dx = target[0] - self.position[0]
        dy = target[1] - self.position[1]
        distance = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
        
        if distance > 0:
            move_distance = self.speed * self.speed_multiplier * delta_time
            if move_distance >= distance:
                self.position = target
            else:
                ratio = move_distance / distance
                self.position = (
                    self.position[0] + dx * ratio,
                    self.position[1] + dy * ratio
                )
    
    def attack(self, target: 'Robot') -> float:
        """Attack another robot with active weapon."""
        if self.health <= 0:
            return 0.0
            
        # Check range
        dx = target.position[0] - self.position[0]
        dy = target.position[1] - self.position[1]
        distance = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
        
        if distance > self.active_weapon.range:
            return 0.0
        
        damage = self.active_weapon.fire() * self.damage_multiplier
        if damage > 0:
            target.take_damage(damage, self)
            return damage
        return 0.0
    
    def take_damage(self, damage: float, attacker: 'Robot') -> None:
        """Take damage from an attack."""
        # Apply shield first
        shield_damage = min(damage, self.shield)
        self.shield -= shield_damage
        damage -= shield_damage
        
        # Apply remaining damage to health
        self.health -= damage
        
        # Record battle experience
        self.battle_memory.append({
            'timestamp': time.time(),
            'damage_taken': damage,
            'attacker_id': attacker.robot_id,
            'attacker_team': attacker.team,
            'position': self.position,
            'health_remaining': self.health
        })
        
        # Keep only recent memories (last 100 events)
        if len(self.battle_memory) > 100:
            self.battle_memory.pop(0)
    
    def switch_weapon(self, index: int) -> None:
        """Switch to a different weapon."""
        if 0 <= index < len(self.weapons):

    def is_alive(self) -> bool:
        """Check if robot is still alive."""
        return self.health > 0
    
    def heal(self, amount: float) -> None:

        # Only switch if significantly needed
        if team_needs[most_needed_role] > 2:

    def learn_from_experience(self) -> None:
        """Learn from past battles and adjust strategy."""
        if not self.battle_memory:

class AssaultRobot(Robot):
    """Specialized assault robot with aggressive behavior."""
    
    def __init__(self, robot_id: int, team: int, position: Tuple[float, float]):
        super().__init__(robot_id, team, position)
        self.role = RobotRole.ASSAULT
        self.aggression_level = 0.8  # 0.0 to 1.0
    
    def decide_action(self, arena: 'Arena') -> None:
        """AI decision making for assault robot."""
        current_time = time.time()
        delta_time = current_time - self.last_action_time
        self.last_action_time = current_time
        
        if not self.is_alive():
            return
        
        # Find nearest enemy
        nearest_enemy = None
        min_distance = float('inf')
        
        for robot in arena.robots:
            if robot.team != self.team and robot.is_alive():
                dx = robot.position[0] - self.position[0]
                dy = robot.position[1] - self.position[1]
                distance = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
                
                if distance < min_distance:
                    min_distance = distance
                    nearest_enemy = robot
        
        # Find nearest objective
        nearest_objective = None
        min_obj_distance = float('inf')
        
        for objective in arena.objectives:
            if not objective.completed:
                dx = objective.position[0] - self.position[0]
                dy = objective.position[1] - self.position[1]
                distance = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
                
                if distance < min_obj_distance:
                    min_obj_distance = distance
                    nearest_objective = objective
        
        # Decision logic based on aggression level
        if nearest_enemy and min_distance < 30 and random.random() < self.aggression_level:
            # Attack enemy if close and aggressive
            self.move_toward(nearest_enemy.position, delta_time)
            
            if min_distance <= self.active_weapon.range:
                damage = self.attack(nearest_enemy)
                if damage > 0:
                    arena.add_particle_effect("hit", nearest_enemy.position)
        elif nearest_objective:
            # Move toward objective
            self.move_toward(nearest_objective.position, delta_time)
            
            # If close enough, contribute to objective
            if min_obj_distance < 5:
                nearest_objective.update_progress(0.1 * delta_time)
                if nearest_objective.completed:
                    self.objectives_completed += 1
        else:
            # Patrol randomly
            random_target = (
                self.position[0] + random.uniform(-20, 20),
                self.position[1] + random.uniform(-20, 20)
            )
            self.move_toward(random_target, delta_time)


class DefenderRobot(Robot):
    """Specialized defender robot with protective behavior."""
    
    def __init__(self, robot_id: int, team: int, position: Tuple[float, float]):
        super().__init__(robot_id, team, position)
        self.role = RobotRole.DEFENDER
        self.defense_position = position  # Position to defend
        self.defense_radius = 15.0
    
    def decide_action(self, arena: 'Arena') -> None:
        """AI decision making for defender robot."""
        current_time = time.time()
        delta_time = current_time - self.last_action_time
        self.last_action_time = current_time
        
        if not self.is_alive():
            return
        
        # Check for enemies in defense radius
        enemies_in_radius = []
        for robot in arena.robots:
            if robot.team != self.team and robot.is_alive():
                dx = robot.position[0] - self.defense_position[0]
                dy = robot.position[1] - self.defense_position[1]
                distance = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
                
                if distance <= self.defense_radius:
                    enemies_in_radius.append((robot, distance))
        
        if enemies_in_radius:
            # Attack closest enemy in defense radius
            enemies_in_radius.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])
            target_enemy, distance = enemies_in_radius[0]
            
            self.move_toward(target_enemy.position, delta_time)
            
            if distance <= self.active_weapon.range:

        else:
            # Return to defense position
            dx = self.defense_position[0] - self.position[0]

# ==================== ARENA CLASS ====================

class Arena:

    def magnitude(self):

        }

        self.title = title
        self.description = description
        self.difficulty = difficulty
        self.objectives = objectives
        self.setup_data = setup_data

            "completed_by": self.completed_by
        }

# ===== FRONTEND UI COMPONENTS =====

class GameBoardUI:
    def __init__(self, board_id: str, rows: int = 8, cols: int = 8):
        self.board_id = board_id
        self.rows = rows
        self.cols = cols
        self.cells = [[None for _ in range(cols)] for _ in range(rows)]
        self.pieces = {}
        self.selected_cell = None
        self.highlighted_cells = []

    def update_board(self, pieces_data: List[Dict]):
        """Update board with new piece positions"""
        self.cells = [[None for _ in range(self.cols)] for _ in range(self.rows)]
        self.pieces.clear()
        
        for piece_data in pieces_data:
            piece = GamePiece(
                piece_data["piece_id"],
                piece_data["piece_type"],
                piece_data["position"],
                piece_data["team_id"]
            )
            self.pieces[piece.piece_id] = piece
            x, y = piece.position
            if 0 <= x < self.rows and 0 <= y < self.cols:
                self.cells[x][y] = piece

    def select_cell(self, position: tuple):
        """Select a cell on the board"""
        self.selected_cell = position
        return self.get_valid_moves(position)

    def get_valid_moves(self, position: tuple) -> List[tuple]:
        """Calculate valid moves from position"""
        x, y = position
        if not (0 <= x < self.rows and 0 <= y < self.cols):
            return []
        
        piece = self.cells[x][y]
        if not piece:
            return []
        
        # Simple move logic (can be extended based on game rules)
        moves = []
        for dx, dy in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:
            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
            if 0 <= nx < self.rows and 0 <= ny < self.cols:
                target = self.cells[nx][ny]
                if not target or target.team_id != piece.team_id:
                    moves.append((nx, ny))
        
        self.highlighted_cells = moves
        return moves

    def render(self) -> str:
        """Render board as string representation"""
        output = []
        for i in range(self.rows):
            row = []
            for j in range(self.cols):
                piece = self.cells[i][j]
                if piece:
                    symbol = piece.piece_type[0].upper() if piece.piece_type else "P"
                    row.append(f"{symbol}{piece.team_id[-2:]}")
                elif (i, j) == self.selected_cell:
                    row.append("[S]")
                elif (i, j) in self.highlighted_cells:
                    row.append("[H]")
                else:
                    row.append("[ ]")
            output.append(" ".join(row))
        return "\n".join(output)

        """Add a message to chat"""
        msg = {
            "id": len(self.messages),
            "sender": sender,
            "message": message,
            "type": message_type,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        self.messages.append(msg)
        
        # Keep only last max_messages
        if len(self.messages) > self.max_messages:
            self.messages = self.messages[-self.max_messages:]

class PerformanceAnalyzer:
    """Machine learning component for analyzing team performance and providing suggestions."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        if ML_AVAILABLE:
            self.regression_model = LinearRegression()
            self.scaler = StandardScaler()
            self.kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
            self.is_trained = False
            self.training_data = []
            self.training_labels = []
    
    def analyze_team_performance(self, team: Team, game_session: GameSession) -> List[str]:
        """Analyze team performance and return suggestions for improvement."""
        suggestions = []
        
        # 1. Check role distribution
        if game_session.settings.roles_enabled and team.players:
            role_counts = self._calculate_role_distribution(team)
            suggestions.extend(self._suggest_role_adjustments(role_counts))
        
        # 2. Analyze performance trends
        if len(team.performance_history) >= 3:
            trend = self._calculate_performance_trend(team.performance_history)
            if trend < -0.1:  # Declining performance
                suggestions.append("Team performance is declining. Consider rotating roles or taking a strategic break.")
            elif trend > 0.1:  # Improving performance
                suggestions.append("Team is improving! Consider maintaining current strategies.")
        
        # 3. Suggest based on game type
        suggestions.extend(self._game_type_specific_suggestions(game_session.settings.game_type))
        
        # 4. Use ML predictions if available
        if ML_AVAILABLE and self.is_trained and len(self.training_data) > 10:
            try:
                ml_suggestion = self._generate_ml_suggestion(team, game_session)
                if ml_suggestion:
                    suggestions.append(ml_suggestion)
            except:
                pass  # ML suggestion is optional
        
        return suggestions if suggestions else ["Keep up the good work! No specific suggestions at this time."]
    
    def _calculate_role_distribution(self, team: Team) -> Dict[Role, int]:
        """Calculate current role distribution in team."""
        distribution = defaultdict(int)
        for player in team.players:
            if player.current_role:
                distribution[player.current_role] += 1
        return dict(distribution)
    
    def _suggest_role_adjustments(self, role_counts: Dict[Role, int]) -> List[str]:
        """Suggest role adjustments based on distribution."""
        suggestions = []
        total_players = sum(role_counts.values())
        
        if total_players == 0:
            return []
        
        # Check for role imbalance
        for role, count in role_counts.items():
            percentage = (count / total_players) * 100
            
            if role == Role.STRATEGIST and percentage > 40:
                suggestions.append("Too many strategists. Consider assigning some players to support or aggressor roles.")
            elif role == Role.SUPPORT and percentage < 10:
                suggestions.append("Consider adding more support players for better team coordination.")
            elif role == Role.AGGRESSOR and percentage > 50:
                suggestions.append("Team may be too aggressive. Balance with more defensive players.")
        
        return suggestions
    
    def _calculate_performance_trend(self, history: List[float]) -> float:
        """Calculate the trend of performance scores."""
        if len(history) < 2:
            return 0.0
        
        # Simple linear trend calculation
        x = list(range(len(history)))
        y = history
        
        if ML_AVAILABLE:
            try:
                # Use linear regression for trend
                x_np = np.array(x).reshape(-1, 1)
                y_np = np.array(y)
                self.regression_model.fit(x_np, y_np)
                return self.regression_model.coef_[0]
            except:
                pass
        
        # Fallback to simple difference
        return (history[-1] - history[0]) / len(history) if history[0] != 0 else 0.0
    
    def _game_type_specific_suggestions(self, game_type: GameType) -> List[str]:
        """Provide game-type specific suggestions."""
        if game_type == GameType.COOPERATIVE:
            return ["Focus on communication and shared objectives.", "Coordinate moves to maximize team synergy."]
        elif game_type == GameType.COMPETITIVE:
            return ["Analyze opponent strategies.", "Consider high-risk, high-reward moves."]
        elif game_type == GameType.TEAM_VS_TEAM:
            return ["Coordinate with team members.", "Identify and exploit opponent team weaknesses."]
        else:  # INDIVIDUAL
            return ["Focus on individual strategy while being aware of team dynamics."]
    
    def _generate_ml_suggestion(self, team: Team, game_session: GameSession) -> Optional[str]:
        """Generate suggestion using trained ML model."""
        try:
            # Prepare features for prediction
            features = [
                len(team.players),
                team.score,
                len(team.performance_history) if team.performance_history else 0,
                sum(team.performance_history[-3:]) / 3 if len(team.performance_history) >= 3 else team.score
            ]
            
            features_array = np.array(features).reshape(1, -1)
            
            # This is a simplified example - in production, you would have more sophisticated ML
            cluster = self.kmeans.predict(features_array)[0]
            
            suggestions_by_cluster = {
                0: "Consider a more aggressive strategy based on team composition.",
                1: "Focus on defensive positioning and risk management.",
                2: "Team is well-balanced. Consider experimenting with new tactics."
            }
            
            return suggestions_by_cluster.get(cluster, "Try adjusting team strategy based on recent performance.")
        except:
            return None
    
    def train_on_history(self, game_sessions: List[GameSession]):
        """Train ML models on historical game data."""
        if not ML_AVAILABLE:
            return
        
        try:
            features = []
            labels = []
            
            for session in game_sessions:
                for team in session.teams:
                    if team.performance_history:
                        # Extract features from team performance
                        team_features = [
                            len(team.players),
                            max(team.performance_history) if team.performance_history else 0,
                            min(team.performance_history) if team.performance_history else 0,
                            sum(team.performance_history) / len(team.performance_history) if team.performance_history else 0,
                            len(session.teams)
                        ]
                        features.append(team_features)
                        
                        # Use average performance as label (simplified)
                        labels.append(sum(team.performance_history) / len(team.performance_history))
            
            if len(features) > 10:
                features_array = np.array(features)
                labels_array = np.array(labels)
                
                # Scale features
                features_scaled = self.scaler.fit_transform(features_array)
                
                # Train models
                self.regression_model.fit(features_scaled, labels_array)
                self.kmeans.fit(features_scaled)
                self.is_trained = True
                self.training_data = features
                self.training_labels = labels
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"ML training error: {e}")

    def add_player_to_team(self, player_id: str, team_id: str, role: Optional[Role] = None) -> bool:

        if player_id not in self.players or team_id not in self.teams:

        player = self.players[player_id]
        team = self.teams[team_id]
        
        # Check if player is already in a team (remove from previous team)
        for existing_team in self.teams.values():
            if player in existing_team.players:
                existing_team.players.remove(player)

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Set

class ExpenseCategory(Enum):
    """Enumeration of supported expense categories."""
    GROCERIES = "Groceries"

@dataclass
class Expense:
    """Represents a single expense entry."""
    id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    user_id: str = ""
    amount: float = 0.0
    category: ExpenseCategory = ExpenseCategory.OTHER
    description: str = ""

        expense.amount = float(data.get("amount", 0.0))

        expense.description = data.get("description", "")
        expense.date = datetime.fromisoformat(data.get("date", datetime.now().isoformat()))
        return expense

class User:
    """Represents a user in the system."""
    id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    name: str = ""
    email: str = ""
    expenses: List[Expense] = field(default_factory=list)
    
    def add_expense(self, amount: float, category: ExpenseCategory, description: str = "") -> Expense:
        """Add a new expense for this user."""
        expense = Expense(
            user_id=self.id,
            amount=amount,
            category=category,
            description=description
        )
        self.expenses.append(expense)
        return expense
    
    def get_total_expenses(self) -> float:
        """Calculate total expenses for this user."""
        return sum(expense.amount for expense in self.expenses)
    
    def get_expenses_by_category(self, category: ExpenseCategory) -> List[Expense]:
        """Get all expenses in a specific category."""
        return [expense for expense in self.expenses if expense.category == category]
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict:
        """Convert user to dictionary for serialization."""
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "name": self.name,
            "email": self.email,

    @classmethod

        user = cls()

    category: ExpenseCategory

Software Development Task:

Please write a budgeting application called BudgetSync that facilitates collaborative budgeting among multiple users. BudgetSync is a web-based application that allows a group of users, such as family members or roommates, to collectively manage their finances. The application provides a shared dashboard for tracking income, expenses, and budget goals, and it supports real-time updates and notifications to keep all users informed and engaged in the budgeting process.
1. Implementation requirements:
   - BudgetSync must allow multiple users to sign up and log in, with each user having a unique profile that includes personal financial data and permissions to access shared budgets.
   - The application should provide a shared dashboard where users can input and categorize their income and expenses. The dashboard should display real-time updates of the total budget, spending breakdowns, and progress towards budget goals.
   - BudgetSync must support the creation of multiple shared budgets, each with its own set of goals and categories. Users should be able to invite others to join a budget and assign different levels of access (e.g., view-only, edit).
   - The application should include adaptive features that adjust based on user feedback and financial data. For example, it should automatically suggest budget adjustments when spending exceeds a certain threshold or when income changes significantly.
   - BudgetSync should provide visual representations of budget breakdowns, such as pie charts and bar graphs, to help users understand their financial patterns. Users should be able to customize these visualizations based on their preferences.
   - The application must include a notification system that alerts users to important budget updates, such as when a budget goal is reached, when a spending limit is exceeded, or when a new user is added to a shared budget.
   - BudgetSync should offer a feedback mechanism where users can provide input on the application's performance and suggest improvements. The system should adapt to this feedback by implementing changes or offering new features in subsequent updates.

            is_income=False
        ).all()
        
        if not transactions:

            monthly_spending[month_key] += t.amount
        
        # Detect anomalies

            current_spending = monthly_spending.get(recent_months[0], 0)

            ).all()

                })

class UserRole(Enum):

class TransactionType(Enum):

class GoalStatus(Enum):

@dataclass

# ==================== Database Interface ====================

class Database(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for database operations."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def save_user(self, user: User) -> None:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_user(self, username: str) -> Optional[User]:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def save_transaction(self, transaction: Transaction) -> None:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_transactions(self, user_id: str) -> List[Transaction]:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def save_budget_category(self, category: BudgetCategory) -> None:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_budget_categories(self, user_id: str) -> List[BudgetCategory]:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def save_goal(self, goal: FinancialGoal) -> None:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_goals(self, user_id: str) -> List[FinancialGoal]:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def save_message(self, message: Message) -> None:
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_messages(self, limit: int = 100) -> List[Message]:
        pass

class InMemoryDatabase(Database):
    """In-memory database implementation for demonstration."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.users: Dict[str, User] = {}

# ==================== Real-time Synchronization ====================

class EventBus:
    """Event bus for real-time synchronization between users."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.subscribers: Dict[str, List[callable]] = defaultdict(list)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    
    def subscribe(self, event_type: str, callback: callable) -> None:
        """Subscribe to events of a specific type."""
        with self.lock:
            self.subscribers[event_type].append(callback)
    
    def publish(self, event_type: str, data: Any) -> None:
        """Publish an event to all subscribers."""
        with self.lock:
            for callback in self.subscribers.get(event_type, []):
                try:
                    callback(data)
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Error in event callback: {e}")

class RealTimeSync:
    """Real-time synchronization manager."""
    
    def __init__(self, database: Database, event_bus: EventBus):
        self.database = database
        self.event_bus = event_bus
        self.user_connections: Dict[str, List[callable]] = defaultdict(list)
        
        # Subscribe to relevant events
        self.event_bus.subscribe("transaction_updated", self._handle_transaction_update)
        self.event_bus.subscribe("budget_updated", self._handle_budget_update)
        self.event_bus.subscribe("goal_updated", self._handle_goal_update)
        self.event_bus.subscribe("message_sent", self._handle_message_sent)
    
    def _handle_transaction_update(self, transaction: Transaction) -> None:
        """Handle transaction updates and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("transaction_updated", asdict(transaction))
    
    def _handle_budget_update(self, category: BudgetCategory) -> None:
        """Handle budget category updates and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("budget_updated", asdict(category))
    
    def _handle_goal_update(self, goal: FinancialGoal) -> None:
        """Handle goal updates and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("goal_updated", asdict(goal))
    
    def _handle_message_sent(self, message: Message) -> None:
        """Handle new messages and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("message_received", asdict(message))
    
    def _notify_users(self, event_type: str, data: dict) -> None:
        """Notify all connected users about an event."""
        for callbacks in self.user_connections.values():
            for callback in callbacks:
                try:
                    callback(event_type, data)
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Error notifying user: {e}")
    
    def register_user_connection(self, user_id: str, callback: callable) -> None:
        """Register a user connection for real-time updates."""
        self.user_connections[user_id].append(callback)
    
    def unregister_user_connection(self, user_id: str, callback: callable) -> None:
        """Unregister a user connection."""
        if user_id in self.user_connections:
            self.user_connections[user_id].remove(callback)

# ==================== Adaptive Feedback Engine ====================

class FeedbackEngine:
    """Engine for providing adaptive feedback and suggestions."""
    
    def __init__(self, database: Database):
        self.database = database
    
    def analyze_budget(self, user_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Analyze budget and provide feedback."""
        categories = self.database.get_budget_categories(user_id)
        transactions = self.database.get_transactions(user_id)
        
        feedback = {
            "warnings": [],
            "suggestions": [],
            "statistics": {}
        }
        
        # Calculate statistics
        total_income = sum(t.amount for t in transactions if t.transaction_type == TransactionType.INCOME)
        total_expenses = sum(t.amount for t in transactions if t.transaction_type == TransactionType.EXPENSE)
        net_balance = total_income - total_expenses
        
        feedback["statistics"] = {
            "total_income": total_income,
            "total_expenses": total_expenses,
            "net_balance": net_balance
        }
        
        # Check for overspending in categories
        for category in categories:
            utilization = (category.spent_amount / category.allocated_amount * 100) if category.allocated_amount > 0 else 0
            
            if utilization > 100:
                feedback["warnings"].append(
                    f"Overspending in '{category.name}': {utilization:.1f}% of budget used"
                )
                feedback["suggestions"].append(
                    f"Consider reducing expenses in '{category.name}' or reallocating funds from other categories"
                )
            elif utilization > 80:
                feedback["warnings"].append(
                    f"High spending in '{category.name}': {utilization:.1f}% of budget used"
                )
        
        # Check net balance
        if net_balance < 0:
            feedback["warnings"].append("Negative net balance this month")
            feedback["suggestions"].append("Consider reducing discretionary spending or increasing income")
        
        # Analyze spending patterns
        if transactions:
            recent_expenses = [t for t in transactions 
                             if t.transaction_type == TransactionType.EXPENSE 
                             and t.timestamp > datetime.datetime.now() - datetime.timedelta(days=30)]
            
            if recent_expenses:
                avg_daily_spending = sum(t.amount for t in recent_expenses) / 30
                feedback["statistics"]["avg_daily_spending"] = avg_daily_spending
        
        return feedback
    
    def analyze_goals(self, user_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Analyze financial goals and provide updates."""
        goals = self.database.get_goals(user_id)
        analysis = []
        
        for goal in goals:
            progress = (goal.current_amount / goal.target_amount * 100) if goal.target_amount > 0 else 0
            
            # Update goal status
            if progress >= 100:
                goal.status = GoalStatus.COMPLETED
            elif goal.deadline and datetime.datetime.now() > goal.deadline:
                goal.status = GoalStatus.FAILED
            else:
                # Calculate days remaining and required daily savings
                if goal.deadline:
                    days_remaining = (goal.deadline - datetime.datetime.now()).days
                    if days_remaining > 0:
                        required_daily = (goal.target_amount - goal.current_amount) / days_remaining
                        if required_daily > 100:  # Arbitrary threshold
                            goal.status = GoalStatus.AT_RISK
            
            self.database.save_goal(goal)
            
            analysis.append({
                "goal_name": goal.name,
                "progress": min(progress, 100),
                "status": goal.status.value,
                "current_amount": goal.current_amount,
                "target_amount": goal.target_amount
            })
        
        return analysis

class VisualizationEngine:
    """Engine for creating budget visualizations."""
    
    @staticmethod

        """Create a pie chart of budget allocation vs spending."""
        if not categories:

        fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 6))
        
        # Allocation pie chart
        labels = [cat.name for cat in categories]
        allocations = [cat.allocated_amount for cat in categories]
        ax1.pie(allocations, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90)
        ax1.set_title('Budget Allocation')
        
        # Spending pie chart
        spendings = [cat.spent_amount for cat in categories]
        ax2.pie(spendings, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90)
        ax2.set_title('Actual Spending')
        
        plt.tight_layout()
        
        # Convert to base64 string
        buffer = BytesIO()
        plt.savefig(buffer, format='png')
        buffer.seek(0)
        image_base64 = base64.b64encode(buffer.read()).decode('utf-8')
        plt.close()
        
        return image_base64
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_bar_chart(categories: List[BudgetCategory]) -> str:
        """Create a bar chart comparing allocation vs spending."""
        if not categories:

        ax.set_ylabel('Amount')
        ax.set_title('Budget Allocation vs Spending')

        return image_base64

class EventBus:
    """Event bus for real-time synchronization between users."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.subscribers: Dict[str, List[callable]] = defaultdict(list)
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    
    def subscribe(self, event_type: str, callback: callable) -> None:
        """Subscribe to events of a specific type."""
        with self.lock:
            self.subscribers[event_type].append(callback)
    
    def publish(self, event_type: str, data: Any) -> None:
        """Publish an event to all subscribers."""
        with self.lock:
            for callback in self.subscribers.get(event_type, []):
                try:
                    callback(data)
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Error in event callback: {e}")

class RealTimeSync:
    """Real-time synchronization manager."""
    
    def __init__(self, database: Database, event_bus: EventBus):
        self.database = database
        self.event_bus = event_bus
        self.user_connections: Dict[str, List[callable]] = defaultdict(list)
        
        # Subscribe to relevant events
        self.event_bus.subscribe("transaction_updated", self._handle_transaction_update)
        self.event_bus.subscribe("budget_updated", self._handle_budget_update)
        self.event_bus.subscribe("goal_updated", self._handle_goal_update)
        self.event_bus.subscribe("message_sent", self._handle_message_sent)
    
    def _handle_transaction_update(self, transaction: Transaction) -> None:
        """Handle transaction updates and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("transaction_updated", asdict(transaction))
    
    def _handle_budget_update(self, category: BudgetCategory) -> None:
        """Handle budget category updates and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("budget_updated", asdict(category))
    
    def _handle_goal_update(self, goal: FinancialGoal) -> None:
        """Handle goal updates and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("goal_updated", asdict(goal))
    
    def _handle_message_sent(self, message: Message) -> None:
        """Handle new messages and notify connected users."""
        self._notify_users("message_received", asdict(message))
    
    def _notify_users(self, event_type: str, data: dict) -> None:
        """Notify all connected users about an event."""
        for callbacks in self.user_connections.values():
            for callback in callbacks:
                try:
                    callback(event_type, data)
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"Error notifying user: {e}")
    
    def register_user_connection(self, user_id: str, callback: callable) -> None:
        """Register a user connection for real-time updates."""
        self.user_connections[user_id].append(callback)
    
    def unregister_user_connection(self, user_id: str, callback: callable) -> None:
        """Unregister a user connection."""
        if user_id in self.user_connections:
            self.user_connections[user_id].remove(callback)

class FeedbackEngine:
    """Engine for providing adaptive feedback and suggestions."""
    
    def __init__(self, database: Database):
        self.database = database
    
    def analyze_budget(self, user_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Analyze budget and provide feedback."""
        categories = self.database.get_budget_categories(user_id)
        transactions = self.database.get_transactions(user_id)
        
        feedback = {
            "warnings": [],
            "suggestions": [],
            "statistics": {}
        }
        
        # Calculate statistics
        total_income = sum(t.amount for t in transactions if t.transaction_type == TransactionType.INCOME)
        total_expenses = sum(t.amount for t in transactions if t.transaction_type == TransactionType.EXPENSE)
        net_balance = total_income - total_expenses
        
        feedback["statistics"] = {
            "total_income": total_income,
            "total_expenses": total_expenses,
            "net_balance": net_balance
        }
        
        # Check for overspending in categories
        for category in categories:
            utilization = (category.spent_amount / category.allocated_amount * 100) if category.allocated_amount > 0 else 0
            
            if utilization > 100:
                feedback["warnings"].append(
                    f"Overspending in '{category.name}': {utilization:.1f}% of budget used"
                )
                feedback["suggestions"].append(
                    f"Consider reducing expenses in '{category.name}' or reallocating funds from other categories"
                )
            elif utilization > 80:
                feedback["warnings"].append(
                    f"High spending in '{category.name}': {utilization:.1f}% of budget used"
                )
        
        # Check net balance
        if net_balance < 0:
            feedback["warnings"].append("Negative net balance this month")
            feedback["suggestions"].append("Consider reducing discretionary spending or increasing income")
        
        # Analyze spending patterns
        if transactions:
            recent_expenses = [t for t in transactions 
                             if t.transaction_type == TransactionType.EXPENSE 
                             and t.timestamp > datetime.datetime.now() - datetime.timedelta(days=30)]
            
            if recent_expenses:
                avg_daily_spending = sum(t.amount for t in recent_expenses) / 30
                feedback["statistics"]["avg_daily_spending"] = avg_daily_spending
        
        return feedback
    
    def analyze_goals(self, user_id: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Analyze financial goals and provide updates."""
        goals = self.database.get_goals(user_id)
        analysis = []
        
        for goal in goals:
            progress = (goal.current_amount / goal.target_amount * 100) if goal.target_amount > 0 else 0
            
            # Update goal status
            if progress >= 100:
                goal.status = GoalStatus.COMPLETED
            elif goal.deadline and datetime.datetime.now() > goal.deadline:
                goal.status = GoalStatus.FAILED
            else:
                # Calculate days remaining and required daily savings
                if goal.deadline:
                    days_remaining = (goal.deadline - datetime.datetime.now()).days
                    if days_remaining > 0:
                        required_daily = (goal.target_amount - goal.current_amount) / days_remaining
                        if required_daily > 100:  # Arbitrary threshold
                            goal.status = GoalStatus.AT_RISK
            
            self.database.save_goal(goal)
            
            analysis.append({
                "goal_name": goal.name,
                "progress": min(progress, 100),
                "status": goal.status.value,
                "current_amount": goal.current_amount,
                "target_amount": goal.target_amount
            })
        
        return analysis

        """Update metrics based on task data."""
        if not user_tasks:
            return
        
        self.total_tasks_assigned = len(user_tasks)
        completed_tasks = [t for t in user_tasks if t.status == TaskStatus.COMPLETED]
        self.total_tasks_completed = len(completed_tasks)
        
        if self.total_tasks_assigned > 0:
            self.task_completion_rate = (self.total_tasks_completed / self.total_tasks_assigned) * 100

            on_time_count = 0
            
            for task in completed_tasks:
                if task.completion_date and task.created_date:

                    total_time += time_diff
                    
                    # Check if completed on time
                    if task.deadline and task.completion_date <= task.deadline:
                        on_time_count += 1
            
            self.avg_completion_time_hours = total_time / len(completed_tasks)

class ReportGenerator(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for report generators."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate a report from data and save to filename."""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        """Get the export format of this generator."""
        pass


class CSVReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in CSV format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: List[Dict], filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate CSV report from list of dictionaries."""
        try:
            if not data:
                return False
            
            # Ensure filename has .csv extension
            if not filename.endswith('.csv'):
                filename += '.csv'
            
            # Get fieldnames from first dictionary
            fieldnames = data[0].keys()
            
            with open(filename, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as csvfile:
                writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=fieldnames)
                writer.writeheader()
                writer.writerows(data)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating CSV report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.CSV


class JSONReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in JSON format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate JSON report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .json extension
            if not filename.endswith('.json'):
                filename += '.json'
            
            with open(filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as jsonfile:
                json.dump(data, jsonfile, indent=2, default=str)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating JSON report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.JSON


class PickleReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in pickle format (binary serialization)."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate pickle report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .pkl extension
            if not filename.endswith('.pkl'):
                filename += '.pkl'
            
            with open(filename, 'wb') as pklfile:
                pickle.dump(data, pklfile)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating pickle report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.PICKLE

class ReportGenerator(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for report generators."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate a report from data and save to filename."""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        """Get the export format of this generator."""
        pass


class CSVReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in CSV format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: List[Dict], filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate CSV report from list of dictionaries."""
        try:
            if not data:
                return False
            
            # Ensure filename has .csv extension
            if not filename.endswith('.csv'):
                filename += '.csv'
            
            # Get fieldnames from first dictionary
            fieldnames = data[0].keys()
            
            with open(filename, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as csvfile:
                writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=fieldnames)
                writer.writeheader()
                writer.writerows(data)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating CSV report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.CSV


class JSONReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in JSON format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate JSON report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .json extension
            if not filename.endswith('.json'):
                filename += '.json'
            
            with open(filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as jsonfile:
                json.dump(data, jsonfile, indent=2, default=str)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating JSON report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.JSON


class PickleReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in pickle format (binary serialization)."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate pickle report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .pkl extension
            if not filename.endswith('.pkl'):
                filename += '.pkl'
            
            with open(filename, 'wb') as pklfile:

            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating pickle report: {e}")

    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:

        with self._lock:

# ==================== Abstract Report Generator ====================

class ReportGenerator(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for report generators."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate a report from data and save to filename."""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        """Get the export format of this generator."""
        pass


class CSVReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in CSV format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: List[Dict], filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate CSV report from list of dictionaries."""
        try:
            if not data:
                return False
            
            # Ensure filename has .csv extension
            if not filename.endswith('.csv'):
                filename += '.csv'
            
            # Get fieldnames from first dictionary
            fieldnames = data[0].keys()
            
            with open(filename, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as csvfile:
                writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=fieldnames)
                writer.writeheader()
                writer.writerows(data)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating CSV report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.CSV


class JSONReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in JSON format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate JSON report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .json extension
            if not filename.endswith('.json'):
                filename += '.json'
            
            with open(filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as jsonfile:
                json.dump(data, jsonfile, indent=2, default=str)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating JSON report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.JSON


class PickleReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in pickle format (binary serialization)."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate pickle report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .pkl extension
            if not filename.endswith('.pkl'):
                filename += '.pkl'
            
            with open(filename, 'wb') as pklfile:
                pickle.dump(data, pklfile)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating pickle report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.PICKLE

class ReportGenerator(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for report generators."""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate a report from data and save to filename."""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        """Get the export format of this generator."""
        pass


class CSVReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in CSV format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: List[Dict], filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate CSV report from list of dictionaries."""
        try:
            if not data:
                return False
            
            # Ensure filename has .csv extension
            if not filename.endswith('.csv'):
                filename += '.csv'
            
            # Get fieldnames from first dictionary
            fieldnames = data[0].keys()
            
            with open(filename, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as csvfile:
                writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=fieldnames)
                writer.writeheader()
                writer.writerows(data)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating CSV report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.CSV


class JSONReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in JSON format."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate JSON report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .json extension
            if not filename.endswith('.json'):
                filename += '.json'
            
            with open(filename, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as jsonfile:
                json.dump(data, jsonfile, indent=2, default=str)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating JSON report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.JSON


class PickleReportGenerator(ReportGenerator):
    """Generate reports in pickle format (binary serialization)."""
    
    def generate(self, data: Any, filename: str) -> bool:
        """Generate pickle report from data."""
        try:
            # Ensure filename has .pkl extension
            if not filename.endswith('.pkl'):
                filename += '.pkl'
            
            with open(filename, 'wb') as pklfile:
                pickle.dump(data, pklfile)
            
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error generating pickle report: {e}")
            return False
    
    def get_format(self) -> ExportFormat:
        return ExportFormat.PICKLE

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
import threading
import uuid

class Database:
    """In-memory database simulation with thread safety"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.users: Dict[str, User] = {}
        self.projects: Dict[str, Project] = {}
        self.tasks: Dict[str, Task] = {}
        self.notifications: Dict[str, Notification] = {}
        self.lock = threading.RLock()
    
    def generate_id(self) -> str:
        """Generate a unique ID"""
        return str(uuid.uuid4())
    
    # User operations
    def add_user(self, user: User) -> bool:
        """Add a user to the database"""
        with self.lock:
            if user.user_id in self.users:
                return False
            self.users[user.user_id] = user
            return True
    
    def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[User]:
        """Get a user by ID"""
        with self.lock:
            return self.users.get(user_id)
    
    def get_user_by_email(self, email: str) -> Optional[User]:
        """Get a user by email"""
        with self.lock:
            for user in self.users.values():
                if user.email == email:
                    return user
            return None
    
    def update_user(self, user_id: str, updates: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
        """Update user information"""
        with self.lock:
            user = self.users.get(user_id)
            if not user:
                return False
            
            for key, value in updates.items():
                if hasattr(user, key):
                    setattr(user, key, value)
            return True
    
    # Project operations
    def add_project(self, project: Project) -> bool:
        """Add a project to the database"""
        with self.lock:
            if project.project_id in self.projects:
                return False
            self.projects[project.project_id] = project
            return True
    
    def get_project(self, project_id: str) -> Optional[Project]:
        """Get a project by ID"""
        with self.lock:
            return self.projects.get(project_id)
    
    def get_user_projects(self, user_id: str) -> List[Project]:
        """Get all projects for a user"""
        with self.lock:
            user_projects = []
            for project in self.projects.values():
                if user_id in project.team_members or user_id == project.manager_id:
                    user_projects.append(project)
            return user_projects
    
    # Task operations
    def add_task(self, task: Task) -> bool:
        """Add a task to the database"""
        with self.lock:
            if task.task_id in self.tasks:
                return False
            self.tasks[task.task_id] = task
            return True
    
    def get_task(self, task_id: str) -> Optional[Task]:
        """Get a task by ID"""
        with self.lock:
            return self.tasks.get(task_id)
    
    def get_project_tasks(self, project_id: str) -> List[Task]:
        """Get all tasks for a project"""
        with self.lock:
            return [task for task in self.tasks.values() 
                   if task.project_id == project_id]
    
    def get_user_tasks(self, user_id: str) -> List[Task]:
        """Get all tasks assigned to a user"""
        with self.lock:
            return [task for task in self.tasks.values() 
                   if task.assignee_id == user_id]
    
    # Notification operations
    def add_notification(self, notification: Notification) -> bool:
        """Add a notification to the database"""
        with self.lock:
            if notification.notification_id in self.notifications:
                return False
            self.notifications[notification.notification_id] = notification
            return True
    
    def get_user_notifications(self, user_id: str, unread_only: bool = False) -> List[Notification]:
        """Get notifications for a user"""
        with self.lock:
            notifications = [n for n in self.notifications.values() 
                           if n.user_id == user_id]
            if unread_only:
                notifications = [n for n in notifications if not n.is_read]
            return sorted(notifications, key=lambda x: x.created_at, reverse=True)
    
    def mark_notification_read(self, notification_id: str) -> bool:
        """Mark a notification as read"""
        with self.lock:

    # Backup and recovery simulation

            self.users[user.user_id] = user
            return True
    
    def get_user(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[User]:
        """Get a user by ID"""
        with self.lock:
            return self.users.get(user_id)

        """Get a user by email"""
        with self.lock:
            for user in self.users.values():
                if user.email == email:
                    return user
            return None
    
    def update_user(self, user_id: str, updates: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
        """Update user information"""
        with self.lock:
            user = self.users.get(user_id)
            if not user:
                return False
            
            for key, value in updates.items():
                if hasattr(user, key):
                    setattr(user, key, value)
            return True
    
    # Project operations
    def add_project(self, project: Project) -> bool:
        """Add a project to the database"""
        with self.lock:
            if project.project_id in self.projects:

        with self.lock:

                    user_projects.append(project)
            return user_projects

    def add_task(self, task: Task) -> bool:
        """Add a task to the database"""
        with self.lock:
            if task.task_id in self.tasks:
                return False
            self.tasks[task.task_id] = task
            return True
    
    def get_task(self, task_id: str) -> Optional[Task]:

"""

# ================ DATABASE MODELS ================

# models.py
from datetime import datetime, date
from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any
from enum import Enum
import json

class UserRole(str, Enum):
    """User role enumeration for role-based access control"""
    ADMIN = "admin"
    MANAGER = "manager"
    TEAM_LEAD = "team_lead"
    DEVELOPER = "developer"
    DESIGNER = "designer"
    ANALYST = "analyst"
    VIEWER = "viewer"

class TaskStatus(str, Enum):
    """Task status enumeration"""
    TODO = "todo"
    IN_PROGRESS = "in_progress"
    REVIEW = "review"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    BLOCKED = "blocked"

class Priority(str, Enum):
    """Task priority enumeration"""
    LOW = "low"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    HIGH = "high"
    CRITICAL = "critical"

class Department(str, Enum):
    """Department enumeration"""
    ENGINEERING = "engineering"
    MARKETING = "marketing"
    SALES = "sales"
    HR = "hr"
    FINANCE = "finance"
    OPERATIONS = "operations"

# ================ DATABASE SCHEMA ================

# Database models using SQLAlchemy-like structure
class User:
    """User model for authentication and authorization"""
    def __init__(self, user_id: str, username: str, email: str, role: UserRole, 
                 department: Department, full_name: str = ""):
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.username = username
        self.email = email
        self.role = role
        self.department = department
        self.full_name = full_name
        self.created_at = datetime.now()
        self.last_login = None
        
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "user_id": self.user_id,
            "username": self.username,
            "email": self.email,
            "role": self.role.value,
            "department": self.department.value,
            "full_name": self.full_name,
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat(),
            "last_login": self.last_login.isoformat() if self.last_login else None
        }

class Project:
    """Project model"""
    def __init__(self, project_id: str, name: str, description: str, 
                 manager_id: str, start_date: date, end_date: date,
                 department: Department, budget: float = 0.0):
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.name = name
        self.description = description
        self.manager_id = manager_id
        self.start_date = start_date
        self.end_date = end_date
        self.department = department
        self.budget = budget
        self.status = "active"
        self.created_at = datetime.now()
        
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "project_id": self.project_id,
            "name": self.name,
            "description": self.description,
            "manager_id": self.manager_id,
            "start_date": self.start_date.isoformat(),
            "end_date": self.end_date.isoformat(),
            "department": self.department.value,
            "budget": self.budget,
            "status": self.status,
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat()
        }

from typing import List, Optional, Dict, Any
from enum import Enum

    """User role enumeration for role-based access control"""
    ADMIN = "admin"
    MANAGER = "manager"
    TEAM_LEAD = "team_lead"
    DEVELOPER = "developer"
    DESIGNER = "designer"
    TESTER = "tester"
    CLIENT = "client"

class TaskStatus(str, Enum):
    """Task status enumeration"""
    TODO = "todo"
    IN_PROGRESS = "in_progress"
    REVIEW = "review"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    BLOCKED = "blocked"

class Priority(str, Enum):
    """Task priority enumeration"""
    LOW = "low"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    HIGH = "high"
    CRITICAL = "critical"

class NotificationType(str, Enum):
    """Notification type enumeration"""
    TASK_ASSIGNED = "task_assigned"
    STATUS_CHANGE = "status_change"
    COMMENT = "comment"
    DEADLINE = "deadline"

class User:
    """User model representing team members"""
    def __init__(self, user_id: str, username: str, email: str, role: UserRole, 
                 department: str, full_name: str):
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.username = username
        self.email = email
        self.role = role
        self.department = department
        self.full_name = full_name
        self.created_at = datetime.now()
        self.is_active = True
        self.notification_preferences = {
            "email": True,
            "in_app": True,
            "push": False
        }
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert user object to dictionary for API responses"""
        return {
            "user_id": self.user_id,
            "username": self.username,
            "email": self.email,
            "role": self.role.value,
            "department": self.department,
            "full_name": self.full_name,
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat(),
            "is_active": self.is_active
        }

class Project:
    """Project model representing a project"""
    def __init__(self, project_id: str, name: str, description: str, 
                 manager_id: str, start_date: date, end_date: date):
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.name = name
        self.description = description
        self.manager_id = manager_id
        self.start_date = start_date
        self.end_date = end_date
        self.budget: Optional[float] = None
        self.status = "active"
        self.tags: List[str] = []
        self.created_at = datetime.now()
        self.team_members: List[str] = []  # List of user_ids
    
    def add_team_member(self, user_id: str) -> bool:
        """Add a team member to the project"""
        if user_id not in self.team_members:
            self.team_members.append(user_id)
            return True
        return False
    
    def remove_team_member(self, user_id: str) -> bool:
        """Remove a team member from the project"""
        if user_id in self.team_members:
            self.team_members.remove(user_id)
            return True
        return False
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert project object to dictionary for API responses"""
        return {
            "project_id": self.project_id,
            "name": self.name,
            "description": self.description,
            "manager_id": self.manager_id,
            "start_date": self.start_date.isoformat(),
            "end_date": self.end_date.isoformat(),
            "budget": self.budget,
            "status": self.status,
            "tags": self.tags,
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat(),
            "team_members": self.team_members
        }

class Task:
    """Task model representing individual tasks"""
    def __init__(self, task_id: str, title: str, description: str, 
                 project_id: str, assignee_id: str, created_by: str):
        self.task_id = task_id
        self.title = title
        self.description = description
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.assignee_id = assignee_id
        self.created_by = created_by
        self.created_at = datetime.now()
        self.updated_at = datetime.now()
        self.due_date: Optional[date] = None
        self.status = TaskStatus.TODO
        self.priority = Priority.MEDIUM
        self.estimated_hours: Optional[float] = None
        self.actual_hours: float = 0.0
        self.tags: List[str] = []
        self.dependencies: List[str] = []  # List of task_ids
        self.comments: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    
    def update_status(self, new_status: TaskStatus, updated_by: str) -> bool:
        """Update task status and track the change"""
        if new_status != self.status:
            self.status = new_status
            self.updated_at = datetime.now()
            # Add to comments as a status change record
            self.comments.append({
                "type": "status_change",
                "user_id": updated_by,
                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "content": f"Status changed from {self.status} to {new_status}",
                "old_status": self.status,
                "new_status": new_status
            })
            return True
        return False
    
    def add_comment(self, user_id: str, content: str) -> None:
        """Add a comment to the task"""
        self.comments.append({
            "type": "comment",
            "user_id": user_id,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "content": content
        })
        self.updated_at = datetime.now()
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert task object to dictionary for API responses"""
        return {
            "task_id": self.task_id,
            "title": self.title,
            "description": self.description,
            "project_id": self.project_id,
            "assignee_id": self.assignee_id,
            "created_by": self.created_by,
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat(),
            "updated_at": self.updated_at.isoformat(),
            "due_date": self.due_date.isoformat() if self.due_date else None,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "priority": self.priority.value,
            "estimated_hours": self.estimated_hours,
            "actual_hours": self.actual_hours,
            "tags": self.tags,
            "dependencies": self.dependencies,
            "comments_count": len(self.comments)
        }
